issues.title: avoid whole-library work on idle sync passes
issues.resolution: The durable engine's leftover-projection checks run up to four times per wake. They now start from an index count of `recovery:` mappings plus the live projection intents, the only facts that can plan local projection. issues.title: avoid full native-tree reconciliation on every worker cold start
issues.resolution: Only the first worker boot of an extension session walks the native tree, captures missing removals and runs the three mapping repairs that read every mapping. A recycled worker missed no bookmark event: Chrome wakes it for each one, staged events wait in the durable inbox, and a failed capture schedules the recovery alarm. Its boot therefore runs the apply-intent repair, flushes the inbox and resumes batch plans. It no longer forces a manual engine pass, which also re-read the whole tree for metadata. It wakes Push at once only when the flush left fresh queue work; otherwise an alarm-reason wake keeps Pull on its own deadline and repairs a missing engine alarm. The three-hour reconcile alarm, the capture-recovery alarm and browser start-up still walk the tree.

issues.title: Investigate transient zero-row second receipt purge in the restored PostgreSQL suite
evidence: First complete isolated run failed second ceiling purge: expected 5, received 0

Failure-only diagnostic now records remaining rows, expiry flags and active test connections without weakening the assertion
issues.resolution: Root cause: the host wall clock, not the purge. PostgreSQL current_timestamp follows the wall clock, and the WSL2 development host steps it backwards. Between 01:32 and 04:50 PDT on 2026-10-23 its journal shows 372 backward steps of 1 to 6.5 s, about one every 30 s (no journal survives from the failing run on 2026-10-22). The ceiling case seeds receipts that expired only one second earlier. A backward step of more than about 1.5 s between the first and second purge makes the five leftover rows unexpired again, so the second purge correctly finds nothing. A step before the first purge would fail it the same way. Lock interference was ruled out: the unit of work never retries, no background purger or other connection uses the test schema, every earlier test awaits or rolls back its transactions, and the purge statement returns exactly the expired, unlocked rows. Fix: every receipt the suite expires (six seeded batches and four ageing updates) is now an hour past its expiry, held in one EXPIRED_AGE constant that explains why. The failure-only diagnostic is removed and the plain 5-row assertion is back.
validation: Journal clock analysis (realtime minus monotonic per entry): 372 backward steps over 50 ms between 01:32 and 04:50 PDT, all but one over 1 s, largest 6.5 s; since 09:00 the steps are under 0.5 s, which is why reruns pass
